editorial:
Imagine being the family failure who can't seem to get anything right, then suddenly finding yourself responsible for a girl who has never seen the outside world. That is exactly what happens to Jay, who meets Daisy, a sweet and naive woman from a psychiatric ward. The vibe is a mix of awkward comedy and heartwarming romance. You get to watch Daisy experience basic things for the first time, like tasting real food or meeting strangers, while Jay tries to fake his way through a family wedding. It feels like one of those quirky stories where two broken people find a way to fix each other through sheer honesty.

What really makes this work is the chemistry between the leads; Daisy's innocence is charming and never feels forced. The pacing is steady, though some parts feel a bit predictable. If you want something light that will make you smile, this is a great pick. It is a cozy watch that doesn't ask too much from you but leaves you feeling good.
endingExplained: After a lot of chaos and family drama, Daisy eventually has to face the truth about her past and her mental health. She spends some time getting the professional help she needs to live a normal life. In the final scenes, Jay shows he has truly changed and waited for her. They reunite in a sweet moment, proving that their bond was real. They end up together, starting a healthy relationship based on trust and love.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves odd-couple romances and feel-good stories.
